S11.01.needs: a notification in the inbox (unread) and a wide window; on phone width the code shows no link to this screen
S11.01.note: On phone width the code has no visible route to the Notifications screen; only the wide-layout bell was found.
steps: Make the app window wide enough for the permanent sidebar (a Mac window, not a phone-width window).
Make sure there is at least one unread notification, so the bell button appears in the header.
Turn on VoiceOver and move across the header button; it should announce "Open notifications, N unread".
Tap the bell. On the Notifications screen, move through each notification row; each should read as one button with its title and time.
Compare with Expected: every control has a name that says what it does.
S11.01.where: Header button "Open notifications, N unread" (only shown in the wide layout with the permanent sidebar), then the Notifications screen

S11.02.note: Section titles are marked as headers in the code; the settings page title comes from the shared shell.
steps: Open Settings from the side menu.
Turn on VoiceOver and use the heading navigation (VO + Command + H) to move between section titles.
Confirm the section names Device, Assistant, Cloud and Support are reached as headings.
Open a settings page such as Settings > Device > General and check its page title is a heading.
Compare with Expected: each screen has a top heading and sections are headings.
S11.02.where: Settings > Device (section title), then the other section titles Assistant, Cloud, Support

S11.05.needs: a paired or unpaired account with the Remote feature enabled (shown only when the companion feature is on)
S11.05.note: The walkthrough is a modal with accessibilityViewIsModal; the code shows Dismiss and Skip buttons, and onRequestClose is wired to skip, so Escape should be the same as Skip.
steps: Open Settings, go to the Remote control section and tap Connections.
Tap "Open Remote" (or "Pair a computer" if not paired).
On the Remote screen, tap the help icon labelled "Show companion walkthrough".
Check that the walkthrough opens as a full-screen dialog with focus inside it; press Tab (or swipe with VoiceOver) and confirm focus stays inside.
Press Escape (or use the "Skip walkthrough" button) and confirm the dialog closes.
Compare with Expected: focus moves into the dialog, stays there, and Escape closes it.
S11.05.where: Settings > Cloud > Remote control > Connections (row "Open Remote" or "Pair a computer"), then the Remote screen, then the help button "Show companion walkthrough"

S11.06.note: No code for restoring focus to the opening control was found. I searched apps/mobile for restoreFocus, returnFocus, "focus restor" and "restore focus" and got no matches.

S11.07.needs: a signed-in account with a working AI reply and VoiceOver on
S11.07.note: The announcement text is not shown on screen; the tester has to listen for it.
steps: Turn on VoiceOver and open a chat.
Focus the "Message input" field and type a short question.
Send it and let the reply finish streaming.
Listen for the short spoken announcements (a "responding" message when the reply starts and an outcome message when it ends) without the focus moving.
Compare with Expected: a short announcement is heard and focus stays where it was.
S11.07.where: Chat screen > "Message input" field > send a message and wait for the reply

S11.09.needs: a signed-in account and a tool request that needs approval
S11.09.note: The approval buttons use the shared labels; the exact button set depends on the approval scope shown.
steps: Open a chat in which the agent runs a tool that needs approval.
Tap the agent activity line whose label starts with "Show agent activity" to expand it.
Read the tool step: it should say its state (running, done, failed or waiting for approval).
For a step waiting for approval, check the buttons labelled "Allow" and "Deny" and the "Decision for" group.
Compare with Expected: each step's state is announced and approve/deny controls have labels.
S11.09.where: Chat screen > a message with agent activity > "Show agent activity" > the tool step or approval row > "Allow" / "Deny" buttons

S11.12.needs: a device with text-size control; the text-size option itself is not in the app
S11.12.note: The code caps font scaling at maxFontSizeMultiplier 2 on settings rows and the chat list title, but there is no in-app text-size control to find.
steps: Change the device text size to a larger setting (the system Text Size or Larger Text option).
Reopen the app and go to Settings > Device > Appearance.
Check that the row labels and values wrap or stay on one line, with values capped at about 200%.
Open the chat list (Chats) and check the header title and subtitle are still readable.
Compare with Expected: text grows up to about 200% and nothing is cut off.
S11.12.where: Settings > Device > Appearance (the text size comes from the device's own text-size setting, not an in-app control)

S11.14.needs: a device that lets the tester turn on Reduce Motion
S11.14.note: The app reads the OS reduce-motion flag through AccessibilityInfo; I did not find a visible in-app switch for it.
steps: Turn on Reduce Motion in the device accessibility settings.
Open the app and go to a screen with a loading or offline indicator.
Check that looping or travelling animations stop or are replaced by a static display.
Compare with Expected: the animations stop or change while Reduce Motion is on.
S11.14.where: Device Reduce Motion setting (not an app control); effect seen on looping or moving animations in the app

S11.15.needs: a microphone and a device with an on-device speech recognizer; the "Open Voice Companion" row is hidden otherwise
S11.15.note: Live voice is also available inside a chat through the chat voice composer, but I did not confirm the button that starts it.
steps: Open Settings > Device > Voice.
Tap "Open Voice Companion" (this row appears only when the on-device recognizer is available).
Start a voice conversation and speak.
Tap the captions button (labelled "Show captions" or "Hide captions") in the voice bar.
Compare with Expected: spoken words appear as live captions while the conversation runs.
S11.15.where: Settings > Device > Voice > "Open Voice Companion", then the live voice bar button "Show captions" / "Hide captions"

S11.16.needs: a microphone and an on-device speech recognizer
S11.16.note: The code shows the transcript while captions are on, but I did not confirm that the voice turns are saved into the chat history.
steps: Open Settings > Device > Voice and tap "Open Voice Companion".
Turn captions on ("Show captions") and have a short spoken exchange.
Read the transcript area (testID live-voice-transcript) that lists each turn.
Go back to the chat that the voice session came from and look for the conversation text.
Compare with Expected: a readable text transcript is kept with the chat.
S11.16.where: Settings > Device > Voice > "Open Voice Companion", then the live transcript shown under the voice bar when captions are on

S11.19.needs: a device or app setting that lets the app use a right-to-left language
S11.19.note: The code applies the right-to-left layout through applyLayoutDirection; I did not confirm which languages are offered or whether a restart is needed.
steps: Open Settings > Device > General.
Tap "App language" and choose a right-to-left language.
Go back and look at the app layout: menus, rows and text should mirror (text aligned to the right, start and end swapped).
If the layout does not change, check whether the app asks you to restart it.
Compare with Expected: the whole layout mirrors correctly.

S11.20.needs: a signed-in account and a chat that can show mixed-direction text
S11.20.note: The code applies right-to-left style per paragraph (directionStyle in MessageContentRenderer); I did not find a left-to-right paragraph style of dir=auto, so the English paragraph may depend on the default.
steps: Open a chat and send a message that has an Arabic or Hebrew paragraph and an English paragraph (or ask for a reply that contains both).
Look at each paragraph in the message bubble.
Check that the Arabic or Hebrew paragraph is right-aligned and the English paragraph is left-aligned.
Compare with Expected: each paragraph is shown in its own direction.
S11.20.where: Chat screen > a message bubble that mixes Arabic or Hebrew text with English text

S11.21.needs: a Japanese, Chinese or Korean input method on the keyboard
S11.21.note: The code shows a multiline field with blurOnSubmit false, and I found no explicit composition handling; Enter is not wired to send in this file.
steps: Switch the Mac keyboard to a Japanese, Chinese or Korean input method.
Open a chat, focus the "Message input" field and type a phrase so it is still being converted (underlined).
Press Enter to confirm the conversion.
Check that the message is not sent and the composed text stays in the field.
Compare with Expected: Enter confirms the composition and never sends the message.
S11.21.where: Chat screen > "Message input" field (a Japanese, Chinese or Korean keyboard)

S11.22.needs: a cloud account with credits that have an expiry date (for the date to appear)
S11.22.note: Dates are formatted with the device locale in cloud-usage; the context-window number is formatted by Intl in plans.
steps: Open Settings and go to the Cloud section, then tap Usage.
Look at any date shown, such as "Expires ..." or "Next expiry ...".
Look at the numbers, such as counts with thousands separators.
Change the device region or language in the device settings, reopen the screen and compare the date and number format.
Compare with Expected: dates and numbers follow the user's locale.

S11.23.needs: a store account (App Store or Google Play); prices come from the store, so they can show only in an app-store build
S11.23.note: Price text comes from the store (nativeIap.priceFor) and is not formatted in the app; the sandbox store may not show prices on a Mac.
steps: Open Settings and go to the Account section, then tap Subscription.
Look at the "Current Plan" section and any plan button showing a price, such as "Upgrade · price".
Compare the currency symbol and number format with the device region.
Compare with Expected: the price shows the right currency symbol and number format.

S11.24.needs: a cloud account with some recap data (ongoing work with follow-ups)
S11.24.note: Other plural strings are in app/(app)/settings/memory-import.tsx, app/(app)/scan.tsx and ArtifactChangesView.tsx, but their entry screens were not traced.
steps: Open Settings, go to the Cloud section and tap Reflect.
Look at the ongoing-work lines that show a follow-up count.
Find a line with exactly one follow-up and one with more than one.
Compare with Expected: "1 follow-up" and "2 follow-ups" follow the language's plural rules.
S11.24.where: Settings > Cloud > Reflect (the follow-up count line in the recap)

S11.27.note: The ledger has no code location for this item and I did not find a specific long-label or translated-copy layout check in apps/mobile; I did not search exhaustively.
